specification_compliance: I1: addons/intelligence/app/workers/clip.py:593-608 adds a 0.0 s anchor unless a scene frame lies below 1 s. _gap_fill_times (clip.py:557-565) splits each gap, including the last anchor to the duration, into ceil(gap/I) equal pieces, so no piece is longer than I. A frame is missing only when extract_frame fails (clip.py:621).

I2: clip.py:610-613 sorts all scene and fill times and thins them at index (i*count)//M before any fill frame is extracted, so at most M extractions run and the stored times are a subset of the thinned list.
I13: config.py:94 sets min_interval to 10 by default. clip.py:479 reads frame_config.min_interval.
I10: database.py:1227-1245 adds loft_candidates_done with default 0 and sets it to 1 for a .loft whose source is 'other' or whose failure count is >= 3.

I11: database.py:491-502 sets the flag to 0 only for a YouTube .loft with loft_fetch_failures < 3, so capped rows keep their value. _migrate_loft_columns (database.py:136) runs before _migrate_vec_clip_if_needed (database.py:146), so the column exists when this update runs.

I9/I10: in loft_media.py:553-571, _failed_result closes the candidates flag without changing the count for a candidates-only fetch. A fetch that also wants the scan or OCR goes through _count_failure, which closes the candidates at the cap (loft_media.py:495-510). An uncounted failure (_note_result false) returns retry_backlog and changes nothing.
potential_unspecified_behavior: When thinning drops a scene frame, its JPEG stays in output_dir. The caller cleans up output_dir, so this has no effect on stored data.
regression_risks: I1 assumes floating-point division in _gap_fill_times keeps every piece at or below I. Any error would be at the ulp level and is not observable in normal use.
test_coverage: I did not inspect the tests under addons/intelligence/tests/ in this verification pass.
